newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium cooked end-1996 books to cut debt-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Belgium cooked end-1996 books to cut debt-WSJ.

text.p: Belgium's Treasury carried out a complex swap with an arm of the central bank to make it appear its net state debt had fallen more than it had, two academics said on Thursday in an article published in the Wall Street Journal Europe (WSJE).

John Laughland and Jean-Michel Paul, writing on the WSJE's opinion page, said they had seen an internal Belgian Treasury memo which made it clear the purpose of the operation was "to reduce the net state debt in order to fulfill the EMU criteria."
No one was immediately available for comment on the article at the Belgian Treasury.
The article was headlined "Belgium cooks its EMU books".

Belgian Budget Minister Herman Van Rompuy and Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said last week total Belgian debt fell to 130.2 percent of gross domestic product at the end of 1996 from 133.7 percent of GDP at the end of 1995.
